newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says anxious to reach tax reform deal.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says anxious to reach tax reform deal.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said he was anxious to resume talks on tax reforms with the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) and that the foundation of a compromise could be reached within weeks.
"I am ready at any time to start negotiating on the basis of the bill that I have proposed," Waigel told the Bild newspaper's Saturday edition.
"If the SPD is serious, we could have the cornerstone of an agreement within 14 days," he said. "That would be a positive signal for the labour market."
Waigel on Friday unveiled his legislative proposals for corporate and income tax cuts of 30 billion marks to create new jobs by stimulating the German economy.
The SPD who want tax cuts to help ordinary workers, opposed Waigel's plan which they see as most benefitting the rich, and no date was set for the resumption of the talks.
Talks between the government and SPD broke up a week ago after the SPD quiet negotiations in sympathy with coal miners protesting government plans to cut coal subsidies.
